bib.title: Aligning Books and Movies: Towards Story-like Visual Explanations by Watching Movies and Reading Books

question: Can books be aligned to their movie releases at shot and sentence level using learned sentence and video-text embeddings?
hypothesis: Learned neural similarities combined by a context-aware CNN and a CRF timeline prior align movies and books better than hand-designed measures or a uniform timeline.
contributions: MovieBook dataset: 11 movie/book pairs with 2,070 annotated correspondences
BookCorpus: 11,038 books for training a sentence embedding
Context-aware CNN combining multiple similarity measures plus a CRF for global alignment
Applications: book retrieval, captioning movies and COCO images with book passages

method.summary: A GRU encoder-decoder sentence embedding (skip-thought) is trained on BookCorpus; an LSTM/CNN video-text embedding is trained on DVS clips; nine similarity measures are stacked and fed to a 3-layer context CNN whose output is the unary term of a chain CRF. CNN and CRF are trained on one movie (Gone Girl) and tested on the other 10.
method.task: movie/book alignment (shot-to-paragraph, subtitle-to-sentence); sentence embedding by unsupervised next/previous-sentence reconstruction

datasets.name: BookCorpus
datasets.size: 11,038 books; 74,004,228 sentences; 984,846,357 words; 1,316,420 unique words; mean 13 and median 11 words per sentence
datasets.split: held-out books used for qualitative neighbours (no sizes given)
datasets.source: free books from the web written by yet unpublished authors; only books with more than 20K words kept; 16 genres (Romance 2,865, Fantasy 1,479, Science fiction 786, Teen 430)

datasets.name: MovieBook
datasets.size: 11 movie/book pairs; 85,238 book sentences; 2,070 annotated correspondences (1,449 dialog, 621 visual); 90 annotator hours
datasets.split: train CNN and CRF on Gone Girl, test on remaining 10 movies
datasets.source: movies with subtitle files and their books, collected by the authors
datasets.preprocessing: books parsed into sentences, paragraphs (indentation) and chapters; subtitles into time-stamped sentences

datasets.name: Movie Description dataset (DVS)
datasets.preprocessing: names replaced by a someone token; clip = mean-pooled frame features (GoogLeNet and hybrid-CNN)

models.name: Skip-thought sentence encoder (GRU)
models.architecture: GRU encoder, two GRU decoders (previous and next sentence) sharing vocabulary matrix V

models.name: Video-text embedding
models.architecture: LSTM sentence encoder, linear map of mean-pooled CNN clip features, cosine score

models.name: Context-aware CNN
models.architecture: 3 conv layers with ReLU and dropout, sigmoid on top, over tensor S(i,j,m) with M=9 measures
models.context: fixed window I in subtitles and J in book (sizes not stated)

training.objective: Sentence model: sum of log-probabilities of previous and next sentences given encoder state. Video-text: bidirectional pairwise ranking loss with margin alpha. Context CNN: cross-entropy. CRF weights learned with latent variables (Schwing et al. 2012).
training.optimizer: Adam for sentence model and CNN; SGD without momentum for video-text model
training.dropout: used in CNN, rate not stated
training.compute: video-text model watches 1,440 movies per day; sentence model reads 870 books per day
training.wall_clock: per movie/book pair: CNN training 2h, CRF training 5h (Table 5)

other.state_pruning: states farther than 1/3 of book length from uniform alignment pruned

inference.samples: one run per movie, no seeds reported
inference.retrieval: CoCoBook: caption from Kiros et al. image-text model used as query; top 10 nearest sentences from a few hundred thousand BookCorpus sentences re-ranked by 1-gram precision of non-stop words; return best plus 2 sentences before and after

parameters.M: 9 similarities: visual, sentence embedding, BLEU1-5, tf-idf, uniform prior

metrics.name: Recall
metrics.definition: for shots with a GT correspondence, GT paragraph is recalled if prediction is at most 3 paragraphs away and shot at most 5 subtitle sentences away

metrics.name: AP
metrics.definition: average precision from recall and precision at multiple alignment thresholds (noisier measure)

baselines: SVM linear combination of similarities as CRF unary
eval.protocol: train on Gone Girl, test on 10 other movies; precision not evaluated because ground truth is not exhaustive

limits: Trained on a single movie (Gone Girl); test is 10 movies, one run, no variance reported.
Ground truth not exhaustive (about 200 correspondences per movie), so precision is not evaluated.
Paper says nothing on licensing, consent or duplicates of BookCorpus.
Many hyperparameters (lr, sizes, margins, window sizes) not stated; sentence model details deferred to Kiros et al. 2015.
CRF does not help for all movies (e.g. Green Mile, Harry Potter recall/AP lower than CNN-3 on AP).
